key_insight: Introduce bond-level PES smoothness metrics (Bond Smoothness Characterization) that reveal non‑physical roughness in ML interatomic potentials missed by standard energy/force errors, and use those metrics to guide architecture and training choices for more physically faithful models.
problem_solved: MLIPs can produce spurious, non‑smooth potential energy surfaces that destabilize downstream simulations while passing conventional energy/force regression tests; existing dynamic probes (e.g., microcanonical MD) are expensive and probe only near equilibrium.
method: Define cheap, local PES smoothness metrics computed from small bond perturbations or short, targeted trajectories (Bond Smoothness Characterization) that quantify curvature and continuity along interatomic coordinates.
Use these metrics as diagnostic scores to compare architectures, hyperparameters, and regularization strategies — prioritizing models with smoother PES even when RMSE is similar.
Validate and calibrate the metrics by correlating them with MD stability and simulation fidelity, demonstrating predictive power and large computational savings versus full MD screening.
impact: Provides a practical, low‑cost evaluation and model‑selection tool so practitioners can design MLIPs that preserve physical smoothness and avoid costly simulation failures, accelerating reliable ML-driven materials and molecular modeling.
visual_elements: Side‑by‑side PES sketches: smooth vs. rough energy curves over a bond coordinate with annotated failure modes.
Pipeline diagram: training candidate MLIP → compute bond smoothness metrics → select/tune architecture → validate with short MD.
Bar chart or scatter plot correlating smoothness metric values with MD stability/failure rate (showing predictive power).
Molecular schematic with bonds color‑mapped by local smoothness score to illustrate spatially resolved diagnostics.
paper_title: From Evaluation to Design: Using Potential Energy Surface Smoothness Metrics to Guide Machine Learning Interatomic Potential Architectures
paper_authors: Ryan Liu, Eric Qu, Tobias Kreiman, Samuel M. Blau, Aditi S. Krishnapriyan
